chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Muṣādif, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning
A man who performed an obligatory salat (prayer) while his hair was tied up; he said: “He repeats his salat (prayer).”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is no harm in a man performing salat (prayer) in Arabian sandals; rather, his salat (prayer) in them is better. It is not permissible for him to perform salat (prayer) in Sindī sandals until he removes them, and salat (prayer) in al-shumishk is not permissible.

key_terms.الشُّمِشْكِ: a type of footwear in which prayer is not permitted
key_terms.النَّعْلِ السِّنْدِيِّ: Sindī sandals in which prayer is not permitted unless removed
key_terms.النَّعْلِ الْعَرَبِيِّ: Arabian sandals considered permissible in prayer
key_terms.مَعْقُوصُ الشَّعْرِ: having the hair tied up or knotted

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying with tied hair or while wearing different types of sandals?
ai.summary: This report gives legal rulings concerning salat (prayer), specifically the state of one’s hair and the type of footwear worn during prayer. It states that an obligatory prayer performed with the hair tied up must be repeated, and it distinguishes between permissible and impermissible kinds of footwear for prayer.
